newsitem.title: MEXICO: Vitro unit sees increased exports.
newsitem.headline: Vitro unit sees increased exports.

text.p: Vitro Vidrio Plano, a subsidiary of Mexican glass giant Vitro, expects to increase exports by 20 percent in 1997, a top company official said.

"We expect to increase exports from Mexico from 50 percent of sales in 1996 to 60 percent of sales in 1997, mainly to South America and the Caribbean," the director general of Vidrio Plano, Pablo Gonzalez Sada, told Reuters in an interview.
In the first three quarters of 1996, Vidrio Plano's exports totalled $137 million, and the company projects $182 million in exports for the year.
Gonzalez Sada said 1997 exports are projected at $218 million.
Vidrio Plano's total sales for the first three quarters equalled 4.157 billion pesos, 70 percent of it dollar-denominated, Gonzalez Sada said.
The parent company Vitro, based in the northern industrial city of Montrerrey, registered export sales of $434 million in the first three quarters of 1996.
Vitro exports to 60 countries, including all of those in Latin America, but plans to grow in South America, especially Brazil, Gonzalez Sada said.

Vidro Plano, which has a Mexican plant that employs 8,125 workers, is exporting glass to Colombia to be processed for automobiles and architectural purposes at its Vetemco affiliate, of which Vidrio Plano gained a controlling interest a few months ago.
"This year we exported more than we had predicted because the Mexican market responded more than we had expected," Gonzalez Sada said.
Domestic automobile parts production in Mexico has fueled much of that unexpected increase, he said.
